note: Admin Theme applies Drupal's admin theme to an arbitrary include/exclude path list. Its whole persistent state is the config object admin_theme.settings with two string keys: paths (Include) and exclude_paths (Exclude), each a newline-separated request_path pattern list. Both ship with the placeholder default '/dummy-path-needed-until-core-issue-2930364-is-fixed' (= match nothing). There is no dedicated settings page (configure route is system.themes_page; fields are injected into /admin/appearance). The switch is performed by the service admin_theme.admin_context which decorates router.admin_context. No permissions, no Drush, no plugins. medium/hard cases set/read these two config keys; cleanup restores the shipped placeholder default.

evals.prompt: In the admin_theme Drupal module, which config object and keys control on which paths the administration theme is applied (and which paths are excluded)?
evals.expected_output: The config object admin_theme.settings has two keys: paths (the Include list) and exclude_paths (the Exclude list), each a newline-separated request_path pattern list.

evals.prompt: What does the admin_theme module let me do that Drupal core cannot, and where do I configure it in the UI?
evals.expected_output: Core can only use the admin theme on node-edit pages; admin_theme lets you apply it to an arbitrary Include list of paths (and an Exclude list). You configure it on the appearance form at /admin/appearance (the Include/Exclude fieldsets); there is no separate settings page.

evals.prompt: How does the admin_theme module actually make Drupal render a page with the administration theme? What core service does it override, and what path syntax do the Include/Exclude fields use?
evals.expected_output: It decorates the core router.admin_context service (AdminThemeAdminContext) so isAdminRoute() returns TRUE on matching paths. The Include/Exclude fields use core request_path condition syntax: one path per line, leading slash, * wildcards and <front>.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the admin_theme module has been configured to apply the administration theme to a particular section. Inspect the live admin_theme.settings configuration and state which path(s) are in the Include list.
evals.expected_output: The Include list (admin_theme.settings:paths) is '/reports' and '/reports/*'. Read it with `drush config:get admin_theme.settings paths`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the admin_theme module excludes a path from the administration theme. Inspect the live configuration and state which path is in the Exclude list.
evals.expected_output: The Exclude list (admin_theme.settings:exclude_paths) is '/admin/content'. Read it with `drush config:get admin_theme.settings exclude_paths`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the admin_theme module to make the administration theme apply to the path /company-dashboard and all of its sub-pages. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set admin_theme.settings:paths to include /company-dashboard (e.g. lines '/company-dashboard' and '/company-dashboard/*'), replacing the placeholder default.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the admin_theme module to exclude the /node/add pages from the administration theme (so content creation forms keep the default theme). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set admin_theme.settings:exclude_paths to include /node/add (e.g. '/node/add' and '/node/add/*'), replacing the placeholder default.
